perceus.title: Perceus: memory guarantees and allocation evidence

memory.title: Native process memory: Fai / Rust / OCaml

perceus: Extend fixed-state, sharing, concurrency and post-burst retention coverage as memory primitives evolve.

Keep balanced ownership, last-use/resource release, uniqueness-based reuse, copy-on-share and shared-value immutability. Fixed state/concurrency must retain bounded live and allocator storage; large buffers must release their mappings at final drop.

Track fixed-state Particles/NBody (#147, #156) independently from per-step compute; preserve strict fallback work in OptionEval/IntEval (#155, #191). Hash-container folds (#544) and standalone list folds (#545) remain focused implementation issues.

Historical ownership-faithful ExprEval/JSON/ListSort/GraphBFS censuses and rejected boxed-RC/layout controls remain in the [investigation archive](https://gist.github.com/Krzysztof-Cieslak/7c1f666874369cacb6fd944ee56f5b96). Diagnostic proportions are not projected speedups.
memory: Extend size and repetition curves around container-capacity thresholds and larger working sets. GraphBFS (#151) has capacity-sensitive jumps and stable post-run RSS at fixed inputs in prior controls; study graph storage separately from allocator retention.

Sieve (#141) uses eight-byte Bool slots versus Rust's one-byte elements. MapSumShared (#153) retains a dense Int array through two traversals. SetDedup (#146) retains only 1,000 distinct values and DictHistogram (#148) only 256 keys despite growing iteration counts.

Separate construction, output and destruction in WordCount (#167), StringBuild/StringSlice (#161, #169), ExprEval (#171) and JsonSerialize (#692); their representations and buffer policies differ across peers.
Establish compatible allocation/live/backing accounting before drawing cross-language live-heap conclusions.
Repeat on additional architectures and retain allocator, GC and host-environment configurations.
runtime: Add independent workload and input holdouts, including varied distributions, Unicode and sharing.
Add matched kernels for application cases with different sorting, hashing, graph/JSON representation or evaluation staging.
Quantify uncertainty for narrow timing differences and expand hardware coverage.

Prioritize array/indexing and scalar costs in CoinChange, MatrixMultiply/FloatMatrixMultiply and Levenshtein (#143, #154, #190, #159); preserve the one-row DP algorithm. NQueens (#164) retains persistent backtracking/sharing, while Collatz/Pi (#165, #172) are mainly scalar work.
Use input-dependent holdouts for MapSum/FoldPipeline (#166, #145): closed-form or fixed-point work reduction and a floor-limited result do not measure sustained instruction throughput.

Continue controlled hashing/probe/growth studies for FibMemo, SetDedup, DictHistogram, UnionFind, GraphBFS and GameOfLife (#142, #146, #148, #157, #151, #160). The application ratios include library and representation differences.

ListSort (#149) merge-state/register-pressure work must preserve stability, comparator order and sharing. Broad layout hoisting and boxed-domain RC-guard controls were rejected; [retained experiments](https://gist.github.com/Krzysztof-Cieslak/7c1f666874369cacb6fd944ee56f5b96) must not be multiplied into the current results.

MergeSort/QuickSort (#144, #152), strings (#161, #167, #169), InterfaceDispatch (#150), OptionTreeFind (#163), ExprEval (#171) and JsonSerialize (#692) need matched components for compiler attribution. TailQuickSort and ASCII/Unicode components are measured separately; the older matched-node tree_lookup fixture remains a follow-up refresh.
Fannkuch (#697) remains staging- and scheduling-sensitive. Existing controls establish neither a sole cache cause nor a promoted fix; retain canonical interleaved observations alongside diagnostics.
Track behavioral implementation work separately, including proper tail calls (#90) and known-closure register calls (#131).
